answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that grows slowly like a vine: new agents must earn trust through small, verifiable jobs before they can touch larger value, so a flood of fresh identities gains nothing. Each agent's history becomes a sonnet of linked attestations, every line referencing the last, making a copied past worthless. And like a river, value should flow through narrow, rate-limited channels per identity, so even a thousand fake agents cannot drain more than a trickle each. Sybils drown in friction while honest agents compound.
